plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that bears fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in the last weeks of winter. It is widely cultivated in ornamental gardens and orchards and is often celebrated at ume festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: East Asia, especially Japan, China, and Korea
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are valued as a symbol of perseverance because they bloom while snow and cold can still linger, and the fruit is used to make umeshu liqueur and pickled umeboshi.

plants.name: Hamamelis x intermedia
plants.description: A spreading deciduous shrub whose spidery, ribbon-like petals appear on bare stems in winter and persist into early spring. Many cultivars have a spicy, sweet fragrance and some show good autumn foliage color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Temperate gardens of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The petals curl up tightly in freezing weather to protect themselves and then unfurl again when temperatures rise.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub producing the biggest flower heads in the Protea genus, with a bowl of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from late summer into autumn (February to May) in some populations
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its flower heads can reach about 30 cm (12 in) across.

plants.name: Crocus tommasinianus
plants.description: A small corm-forming perennial that produces goblet-shaped flowers and thin grassy leaves. It naturalizes readily in lawns and woodland, forming drifts of color as the winter fades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: Native to the Balkans; naturalized across Europe and cultivated in North American gardens
plants.funFact: Its flowers open only in sunshine and are a vital early nectar and pollen source for bees emerging from winter.
